prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” universal roof contractor — the best one for you depends on your exact address, roof type, budget, and whether you want shingles or a metal/ tile system. I can find top-rated, hurricane-rated roofers near you if you give your Miami ZIP code. Meanwhile, here’s how to identify the right contractor and a checklist of what to require for a hurricane-rated roof replacement.

What to require for a hurricane-rated roof replacement
- Miami‑Dade/Florida code compliance: Products and methods must meet the Florida Building Code and Miami‑Dade County approvals. Ask for Miami‑Dade Notice of Acceptance (NOA) or other product approvals for materials used.  
- High-wind systems: Components (shingles/tiles/metal panels, underlayment, flashing, fasteners, adhesives) must be tested and rated for high-wind/uplift resistance.  
- Manufacturer certification: Prefer contractors certified by major manufacturers (e.g., GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Preferred, CertainTeed Select) — this improves warranty coverage.  
- Proper fastening and attachment: Nail type, pattern, and deck fastening must match code and NOA requirements (e.g., ring‑shank nails, adequate deck attachment).  
- Secondary water barrier: Use code-approved underlayment/secondary waterproofing per local requirements.  
- Permits & inspections: Contractor must pull permits and arrange inspections; do not accept waiving permits.  
- Insurance and licensing: Verify the contractor’s Florida license and that they carry general liability and workers’ comp. Request their license number and insurance certificates.  
- Warranties: Get both the contractor’s workmanship warranty and manufacturer product warranty in writing.

How to vet and compare contractors
- Check Miami‑Dade product approvals and Florida Building Code references on proposals.  
- Verify license: Florida DBPR / Construction Industry Licensing Board (CILB).  
- Read recent local reviews (Google, Yelp, Angi) and ask for 3 local references for hurricane-rated replacements done in the last 2–3 years.  
- Ask for a written, line‑item estimate (materials, labor, removal, permit costs). Compare 3 bids.  
- Confirm who does the work: company crews vs. subcontractors; obtain timeline and debris‑removal plan.  
- Ask whether they provide the prospect of an official wind mitigation inspection and documentation for insurance discounts.

Red flags to avoid
- Requests for full payment up front (a reasonable deposit is typical, but not full payment).  
- “We’ll skip the permits” or “no inspection required.”  
- No written contract or vague warranty language.  
- Very low estimate relative to others (could indicate cut corners).  
- Unable to provide proof of insurance, license number, or local references.

Where to look for reputable contractors in Miami
- Miami‑Dade County building/permit records and product approvals (NOA).  
- Florida DBPR license lookup.  
- Google Business, Angi (Angie’s List), BBB, and local Facebook community groups for homeowner referrals.  
- Manufacturer contractor locators (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed, TAMKO).

If you want, I can:
- Find and shortlist 3–5 highly rated, hurricane-rated roof replacement companies in Miami with links, reviews, and notes on certifications — give me your ZIP code or neighborhood.  
- Or review quotes/proposals you’ve received and point out concerns.

Which would you like me to do?
